interactions.summary: Jiang rejects the idea that God lacks free will, then lets the class test several answers for why God grants human freedom, including an omnipotent experiment model, a maze-like contrast model, and the claim that humans receive agency because they are made in God's image.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led classroom exchange with multiple student replies

claims.claim: Jiang immediately rejects the suggestion that God lacks free will, while a student clarifies the issue by saying the point is that God cannot sin.
A student proposes that because God is omnipotent he can choose to grant freedom to people in order to see how they react, almost as an experiment.
Jiang sharpens that proposal into a provocation that would make human life look like mice in a lab being tested by God.
Another student argues that if God wants humans to reach him, there must also be a genuine possibility of not reaching him so the journey has real contrast.
A student suggests that God made human beings in his own image and therefore wanted them to possess agency like his.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang forces the class to face the ugliness of the experiment idea by turning humanity into lab mice.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we're like mice in a lab
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The provocation pressure-tests whether the class's explanation of divine freedom is morally and theologically acceptable.

signature_moments.moment: The maze image turns salvation into a path whose point depends on a real possibility of failure.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you have this like maze and you want the mouse to come to you
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It translates abstract free-will talk into a vivid picture of contrast, destination, and testing.

signature_moments.moment: Agency is justified by likeness to God himself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: God made men in his own image
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's cleanest positive answer for why human freedom matters in the first place.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Used here to argue that God's total power includes the choice to grant freedom of choice to humans.
The human likeness to God that one student offers as the reason people are given meaningful freedom.
The creation formula invoked to justify why humans would inherit agency analogous to divine action.

chronology_notes.note: This packet stays inside the same June 15 classroom debate over why free choice exists and does not mark a dated shift across Jiang sources.
